03ã THE NETWORK LOOP

From one key to independent supply, in three steps.

You bring the request. Miners compete to serve it with their own models. Validators measure them the way a customer would, and the network rewards what works.

See the APIâ
01

Call

Use one Terza key with the SDKs you already know. The maximum cost is reserved before anything is sent.

02

Serve

Approved, on-chain miners serve your request through their own upstreams. Every gateway request to a miner is signed.

03

Verify

Usage receipts are checked against what was delivered, and validators score miners with paid probes that look like your traffic.

04ã BUILT FOR BUILDERS

Your next idea. Many models behind it.

Point your existing client at Terza. Same request shapes, one key, and a choice of independent supply for every model.

05ã ACCOUNTABILITY

Every charge is checked before you pay it.

Miners report usage; the gateway compares it with what was actually delivered. Implausible receipts are rejected, failures are never charged, and media is billed on measured output.

01 Â· RECEIPTS

Usage is checked, not trusted

Tokens beyond the request size or the delivered text are rejected, and the reason is recorded.

02 Â· MEDIA

Billed on what was measured

Duration, resolution and count are measured by the gateway itself; non-conforming output costs nothing.

03 Â· FAILURES

Failures cost nothing

A failed request releases its whole reservation and counts against the miner, not you.

06BY DESIGN

Built so you only pay for what you get.

Facts about how Terza Inference routes, checks and settles every request. Design facts, not performance claims.

THE DECENTRALIZED POST-TRAINING PLATFORM

Take intelligence further.

Generate training data for your tasks, evaluate your models, and train them with reinforcement learning. Powered by independent GPUs and a network that discovers what models can still learn.

Open App Explore the research

Network

Reliquary distributes RL rollout generation across independent GPUs, from consumer hardware to datacenter machines. Each contributor chooses which prompts to test and runs the same model at their own pace.

Every contribution is verified against the published checkpoint before selected groups can be used for training.

Contributing takes an NVIDIA GPU with 24 GB of memory or more. Requirements

Read the network guide See live network activity

Learning signal discovery

Generating more responses isn’t enough. The challenge is finding prompts that still help a model learn.

In GRPO, when all attempts succeed or all fail, there’s no reward contrast to learn from. The useful prompts are those where some attempts succeed and others fail.

Reliquary’s contributors compete to find these prompts, directing compute toward useful training signals rather than simply generating more data.

Learning signal. 3 of 8 attempts solved, so the update can favor the better ones.

How GRPO scores this group
Reward
100101001 if solved, 0 if not
Group mean
3 / 8 = 0.375the group-average line
Advantage
1 − 0.375 = +0.6253 solved, above the line
0 − 0.375 = −0.3755 failed, below the line

Advantage = reward − group mean. GRPO then divides each advantage by the spread of the group, which changes neither the signs nor the zeros.

Learnable: 3 of 8 attempts solved, group mean 0.375. The update makes the 3 solved attempts more likely (advantage +0.625) and the 5 failed ones less likely (advantage −0.375). Learning signal.

Research

We study how to post-train models on rollouts from independent GPUs: which prompts carry learning signal, how to check work we do not run, and what the resulting models show. Each result is published with its setup and its limits.

Released model · Sep 2026

Reliquary-4B

Qwen3-4B-Base, trained with reinforcement learning on about 6.6 million rollouts, all generated by independent contributors. The trainer and validator are centralized.

Compared with its base model. Sampled pass@1, 8 samples per problem, T = 1.0.
